notebooks.title: Foundational Constraints in AI Metareasoning
notebooks.summary: AI metareasoning is currently bifurcated: established 'resource partition' models focus on computational efficiency, while emerging epistemological frameworks like 'Equity Bias' advocate for making foundational assumptions explicit and contestable. Current LLMs can support the transparency of these assumptions, but autonomous self-correction of foundational premises remains unproven.
notebooks.findings:
Traditional metareasoning focuses on the 'partition problem' of resource allocation rather than epistemic self-correction. [source-27c3e6da377b41e4]

Epistemic inclusion frameworks offer a strategy for making AI foundational assumptions 'contestable' rather than invisible. [source-443f82fd8d5543a6]
notebooks.limitations: Evidence remains concentrated in theoretical frameworks or external design methodologies; there is no documented empirical proof of an LLM autonomously identifying a foundational logical flaw in its own reasoning architecture and developing a superior replacement without human intervention.
notebooks.next_questions: Can the 'Equity Bias' framework's 'Equity Archaeology' methodology be implemented as an automated internal loop within an LLM's chain-of-thought to detect invalid premise propagation?
notebooks.reason: Revising the notebook to incorporate the 'Equity Bias' framework provides a clearer pathway to addressing the project's question on assumption identification.

notebooks.title: Provisional Analysis: CRASH Agent Architecture and Industrial Generalizability
notebooks.summary: The Cognitive Reasoning Agent for Safety Hazards (CRASH) demonstrates a successful paradigm for processing heterogeneous incident reports. By incorporating insights from graph-augmented LLM agent frameworks like GALA+ and data quality investigations in incident response, we analyze pathways for extending these architectures to non-standardized industrial domains.
notebooks.findings:
Cognitive reasoning agents utilize unified representations to process heterogeneous safety incident reports. [source-ed95ef98c2374a5f]

Graph-augmented LLM agentic frameworks can bound exploration and refine root cause analysis across complex service dependencies. [source-c74a69eb8eff48c7]
notebooks.limitations: Direct empirical validation remains centered on autonomous vehicle and microservice benchmarks; broad application to heavy industrial domains requires robust handling of unstandardized data quality.
notebooks.next_questions: How can graph-guided investigation frameworks bridge the telemetry gap in non-standardized industrial environments?
notebooks.reason: Revised notebook incorporating broader evidence on graph-augmented LLM agents and incident data quality to assess industrial generalizability.

notebooks.title: AI Dependence and Reduced Autonomy in Athletes
notebooks.summary: Recent cross-sectional evidence indicates that dependence on AI training recommendations is positively associated with body signal outsourcing, which correlates with reduced self-regulation, decision hesitation, and diminished training self-efficacy.
notebooks.findings:
AI training recommendation dependence is positively associated with body signal outsourcing tendency in athletes. [source-18d0eec713c84bb4]

Body signal outsourcing links to a reduced sense of self-regulation and increased training decision hesitation. [source-d9addfec171d4b5d]
notebooks.limitations: The findings are derived from cross-sectional questionnaire data, meaning causal directions remain provisional and require longitudinal tracking.
notebooks.next_questions: What are the longitudinal impacts of sustained AI training recommendation dependence on long-term athlete autonomy and self-regulation?
notebooks.reason: Revising notebook nb-emergent-prefs-001 using newly incorporated evidence from Chen (2026) to detail the serial association model.

notebooks.title: Computational Creativity and Active Inference in Problem Formulation
notebooks.summary: Integrating active inference frameworks and drift-diffusion models to examine cognitive effort and problem selection mechanisms in autonomous agents.
notebooks.findings: High-level Bayesian brain theories frame cognitive effort as resolving conflict between habits and optimal policies, which can be modeled using active inference combined with evidence accumulator models. [source-6ee93795fbf2497c]
notebooks.limitations: Findings rely on theoretical models and behavioral task fits rather than fully general autonomous scientific discovery environments.
notebooks.next_questions: How do epistemic value formulations scale to open-ended research environments without predefined task structures?
notebooks.reason: Revised notebook integrating newly collected source evidence regarding active inference and cognitive effort.

notebooks.title: Explicit Falsification in AI-Generated Science
notebooks.summary: An examination of whether autonomous multi-agent systems can employ explicit falsification agents to test and challenge research assumptions.
notebooks.findings: Autonomous scientific research systems can be structured around explicit falsification agents to identify and verify potential discoveries. [source-29b2590d54274ad4]
notebooks.limitations: Findings rely on early-stage framework demonstrations and require further empirical testing across diverse reasoning domains.
notebooks.next_questions: How do automated agents handle domain-specific boundary conditions when generating falsification hypotheses?
notebooks.reason: Synthesizes collected evidence regarding Baby-AIGS and falsification-driven autonomous agent architectures.

notebooks.title: Flow-State as an Emergent Preference
notebooks.summary: Evidence suggests that users have a persistent, stable preference for 'flow' states—defined as a balance between task difficulty and skill. AI systems aiming to support this preference must avoid disrupting this state with static or intrusive interventions.
notebooks.findings: Users exhibit a stable preference for tasks that balance difficulty and skill level, a state defined as 'flow'. [source-f201ddb5b6e54d8d]
notebooks.limitations: The current evidence links flow to user satisfaction but does not prove it is an 'unprogrammed' preference emerging from memory reinforcement learning in autonomous agents.
notebooks.next_questions: Does long-term interaction with an AI agent create stable 'flow-seeking' behavior patterns in the agent itself, or only the user?
notebooks.reason: Synthesis of existing sources regarding flow theory and cognitive augmentation.

values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.
